- Java 21, Spring Boot 3.3.5, Maven pom.xml

- REST: POST/GET/PUT /api/tickets, GET /api/tickets/{id}, PUT /api/tickets/{id}/status, POST /api/tickets/{id}/comments

- Jakarta validation, ProblemDetail error responses, 409 on invalid transitions
- CORS for localhost:5173 and 3000
- H2 file: jdbc:h2:file:./data/tickets
- Tests: TicketStateMachineTest (4 tests), TicketStateMachineIntegrationTest, TicketControllerIntegrationTest
- test application.properties with H2 mem
- README.md and .gitignore (target/, data/)

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The test `filterByStatusReturnsOnlyMatchingTickets` fails because three OPEN tickets were returned instead of one.

The test logic itself appears flawed. It creates two OPEN tickets, closes one, then expects only one OPEN result. The extra ticket likely comes from the second OPEN record not being properly closed or filtered out.

MockMvc transactions may not roll back between test methods in the same Spring context. The closeTicket transition logic was also traced and appears correct.

The extra OPEN ticket likely stems from data leaking between test methods. `@Transactional` should roll back each test, yet `@Commit` annotations or test ordering may be preventing proper isolation.

MockMvc may run inside a separate transaction or thread than the test method's `@Transactional` rollback. Data committed during MockMvc requests would then leak across test methods, causing the extra OPEN ticket.

The three OPEN tickets match the sum of earlier test creations: one from `createTicketReturns201WithOpenStatus`, one from `searchByKeywordReturnsMatchingTicket`, and two from `filterByStatusReturnsOnlyMatchingTickets`. The `blankTitleReturns400` test added zero tickets. This confirms data is accumulating across test methods rather than rolling back.

The simplest fix is to add a `@BeforeEach` method that clears the ticket repository before each test, or to use `@Sql` cleanup scripts to reset the database between test methods.

The root cause is now clear. `TicketService` carries `@Transactional`, so MockMvc requests inside the test transaction commit their changes. These commits survive the outer test rollback, causing data to accumulate across test methods.

MockMvc requests trigger the service’s `@Transactional`, which suspends the test transaction and spawns a new one that commits independently. This explains why data leaks across test methods despite the outer rollback. The cleanest fix is to add a `@BeforeEach` method that clears the ticket repository before each test.

MockMvc likely runs in a separate thread that does not join the test transaction. The chosen fix is a `@BeforeEach` method that deletes all tickets from the repository before each test. This cleanup will be added to every integration test class.

I will fix the failing test by adding `@BeforeEach` cleanup to both integration test classes. Then I will return the complete list of all files created. I considered installing Maven or adding a Maven wrapper, but the user only requested writing the files.
